subject: Do the ten new voices work on text unlike what they were trained on?
why: Every earlier number came from FLORES, which is also the corpus these voices were distilled on. Held-out FLORES rows are held out by row, not by domain, so they cannot answer whether a voice generalises. This repeats the measurement on Tatoeba: short user-contributed conversational sentences, a different domain and register, sampled with a fixed seed from 25k-830k candidates per language.
method: 16 sentences per voice, rendered by the numpy runtime, transcribed by Whisper small, CER against the source.
headline: They generalise. Seven of eleven packages score BETTER on unseen conversational text than on the corpus they were trained on, and none collapses. The worst domain shift is Czech at +0.037.

notable.german: 0.097 on FLORES, 0.032 on Tatoeba. German looked like the weakest student in the set; it was the test text, not the voice. FLORES news prose is dense with proper nouns that ASR mangles regardless of the speaker.
notable.tiny_511k: 0.045 on Tatoeba against the full 1.56M model's 0.032. A third of the parameters still generalises to unseen text.
notable.regressions: Czech +0.037, Romanian +0.031 and French +0.030 got worse out of domain. All three remain far below the 0.261 of the currently published Vietnamese voice, but they are the three to listen to first.

caveats: 16 sentences per voice. Directional, not precise.
Tatoeba sentences are shorter and simpler than FLORES, which flatters every voice; the domain SHIFT per voice is the meaningful signal, not the absolute.
Still intelligibility only. No listener has heard any of these.
